correctness.rationale: Theorem D of arXiv:2610.03619v1 supplies a quantitative Lipschitz cohomology decomposition. Exact telescoping, the balance bound for the digit cocycle, and the unit diameter of the symbolic metric give \(W_\theta(\eta_{x,n},\mu_\alpha)\le1/[n(1-\theta)^3]\). The matching upper bound follows from the triangle inequality and the equality between permutation cost and Wasserstein distance for equal-weight empirical measures. Balance and the nonintegral mean \(n\alpha\) force both adjacent digit counts for every \(n\); the digit observable then gives the lower bound \(1/n\). No finite experiment or asymptotic-only argument is used.
